consensus_summary: Consensus primary meaning is right standing before God (especially Christ's righteousness imputed/credited by faith apart from works) together with conformity to God's moral character and standard; symbolic garment/breastplate imagery is common; mechanisms remain debated (imputed vs. infused/transformative, covenant faithfulness, ethical/social justice).
book_summary: Righteousness is right-living: God Himself is right-living by definition, and for those under His authority it is the doing of His commandments (the law kept), worn as the garment of righteous acts. It is given and reckoned by grace (Romans 4 excludes wage-work that would put God in debt, not obedience itself), but the gift never renames wrong-living right.
consensus_core_identification: right standing before God plus conformity to His standard (prominently as imputed gift through faith)
book_core_identification: right-living (doing of God's commandments), given and reckoned by grace without renaming wrong-living as right
boundary_disagreement: Whether imputed/reckoned status alone can constitute righteousness while wrong-living continues (consensus primary often yes, with living as subsequent fruit/evidence; book no—the gift never renames wrong-living right, and he who does righteousness is righteous).
material_contradiction: None at the shared core category of God-measured rightness applied to persons by grace; the difference is boundary precision and priority of living versus status.
rationale: Minimum cores share the same general referent (divine rightness/conformity applied to God and to persons under Him, involving both gift/reckoning and moral content). The book preserves that category while materially narrowing its conditions and reclassifying pure forensic-status cases (and the common 'standing primary, living as fruit' framing) so that actual commandment-keeping becomes definitional rather than merely evidential. This is boundary refinement, not replacement of the central referent or a novel category outside the consensus alternatives.
strongest_objection: The book's own citations (esp. Rom 4:4-8 and Phil 3:9) are classically read as establishing a primarily forensic 'without works' core that the entry subordinates to right-living, risking an artificial narrowing that underplays the very texts it prints.
